messages:
liz-sales: Polaris Analytics is stuck on the POC step where they POST to /v1/generate. They get a 403 with "invalid_org_binding" and later saw "insufficient_scopes" when trying embeddings. Demo in 50m.

omar-ps: Do they share the exact curl or SDK snippet? Often this is caused by accidentally sending a prod org header or using a key with limited scopes.

liz-sales: They pasted this from their staging env: 
```bash
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer sk_demo_polaris01" -H "X-Redwood-Org: org-polaris-prod" -d '{"input":"hello"}' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate
```
They said someone copied headers from a prod example by mistake.

hua-eng: That explains invalid_org_binding. Runtime compares the key's embedded org_id claim to the X-Redwood-Org header (if present). If they differ -> 403 invalid_org_binding. Quick confirmation: is sk_demo_polaris01 bound?

anna-ops: Inspecting now: `redwood keys inspect sk_demo_polaris01` -> {"key":"sk_demo_polaris01","org_id":"org-polaris-demo","scopes":["generate"],"bound":true} (inspected by anna-ops).

omar-ps: Bound=true is the smoking gun. Also missing "embed" scope explains the embeddings 403/insufficient_scopes. Two fast options: 1) ask them to remove or correct the X-Redwood-Org header, or 2) create a short-lived unbound key or a multi-scope demo key.

liz-sales: They want the least amount of friction. Which is fastest?

hua-eng: Easiest is to remove the header in their staging snippet. Example: 
```bash
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer sk_demo_polaris01" -d '{"input":"hello"}' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate
```
If they must run embeddings in the same live session, ops can issue sk_temp_polaris_multi with scopes ["generate","embed"] and a 45m TTL.

anna-ops: I can create a multi-scope demo key for 45m with ops approval and log the audit. Will we also need to increase concurrency? They plan to run ~40 parallel requests.

omar-ps: Demo keys default to low concurrency. 40 parallel calls likely trigger 429s. Recommend two mitigations: client retry with exponential jitter (100ms base, 3 retries) OR ops bump soft concurrency for the org for the demo window.

liz-sales: Please create the multi-scope temp key and bump concurrency for 60 minutes. I'll pass to the customer. Also, Polaris asked about SSO and whether we can bind keys to SSO sessions for audit continuity.

hua-eng: We don't bind API keys to SSO sessions directly. Best practice: use org-bound or project-bound keys and correlate key usage to SSO user actions via audit logs and console events. For SSO-centric flows we recommend using short-lived service tokens issued by an internal auth flow that maps to the user's SSO identity. I'll draft a short note for the security questionnaire.

anna-ops: Creating temporary key now under tag `demo/polaris/multi-45m`. Recording audit entry.

redwood-bot: New API key created: sk_temp_polaris_multi (expires in 2700s) — created by anna-ops — scopes:["generate","embed"] — reason: Polaris demo (45m) — audit_id: audit_2115560052_pol

liz-sales: Sharing key with customer. They confirm invalid_org_binding is gone but now report occasional 429s when they burst 40 concurrent calls.

omar-ps: That's expected. Give the retry snippet and ask them to add jitter. Example suggestion: exponential backoff with full jitter, base 120ms, 4 attempts. Also offer to keep concurrency raised for the first 30m of the demo.

anna-ops: Raised concurrency for org-polaris-demo to 50 for 60m and set an alert to revert after window. Audit noted.

redwood-bot: Action: concurrency increased for org-polaris-demo (60m). Audit recorded: audit_2115560120_concurrency.

liz-sales: Polaris ran the test again — 429s dropped significantly and embeddings worked with the new key. They said latency looked great and asked a follow-up: will demos ever be billed for token count or concurrency?

hua-eng: For official demo windows we don't bill ad-hoc spikes. Production usage is billed per-token (and Dedicated has reserved capacity pricing). For any long-term or high-throughput evaluation, pricing team will provide a quote.

omar-ps: Also add in the security questionnaire: demo key handling and audit proof. Polaris wanted a blurb about key rotation and auditability. Hua, can you draft 2 bullets?

hua-eng: Draft: "• Demo keys are short-lived and can be org- or project-bound and scoped to specific endpoints. Temporary unbound or multi-scope demo keys are issued with Ops approval and logged. • Production keys should be bound for tenant isolation and rotated regularly; correlate usage with SSO via audit exports for compliance." Send that to me and I'll paste in the questionnaire.

anna-ops: Exported audit for sk_temp_polaris_multi and attached to security questionnaire. Key will auto-expire in 45m.

liz-sales: Polaris confirmed POC passed and requested pricing & a brief note about prod key best practices. I'll send follow-up. Great work team — closing thread unless they reopen. :tada:
